chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not forget the two obligators,' or he said, 'Upon you are the two obligators, at the end of every prayer.' I asked: 'And what are the two obligators?' He said: 'Ask Allah for Paradise and seek refuge in Allah from the Fire.'
ai.seo_question: What are the two obligators (al-mujibbatayn) to be recited after every prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) emphasizes the 'two obligators' (al-mujibbatayn) as essential post-prayer supplications, instructing believers to consistently ask Allah for Paradise and seek refuge from the Hellfire. This directive highlights the dual nature of worship—hope and fear—ensuring that the spiritual momentum of the prayer extends into daily life through deliberate dhikr and du'a. In Shia tradition, this practice is viewed as a means of securing the soul's ultimate destination by balancing the desire for divine reward with the awareness of divine justice.
